analysis.text:
By a Final Decree dated 5 May 2018, entered in partition case bearing No. 3535/P of the District Court of Nugegoda, Ajith Silva was allotted all that allotment of land marked Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 dated 2 March 2010, made by A. C. Perera, Licensed Surveyor, of the land called Kahatagahawatte, bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda, containing in extent 15 perches.

Ajith Silva, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 December 2018, attested by P. C. Nonis, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot 2 depicted in Plan No. 1616 to Prabash Silva, the elder son of Ajith, subject to the life interest of the donor, and subject to the condition that Prabash shall not sell, mortgage or otherwise deal with the land, but may enjoy the produce thereof during his lifetime. On the death of Prabash, the property shall devolve free of all conditions to Subash, the younger son of Ajith Silva.

Ajith had three children, namely Prabash, Subash and Shehani, by his second marriage to Yamuna. Ajith had another daughter named Kushani from his first marriage to Sumana.

Ajith Silva died intestate on 2 March 2019, and Prabash Silva died intestate on 2 June 2019.

Prabash had two daughters, namely Sunali and Bimali, by his first wife Sheela, and two sons, namely Brian and Rian, by his second wife Linda. Sheela died intestate on 5 August 2019. Brian married Sara and thereafter died in an accident on 25 September 2021 without having children. Sunali died on 10 October 2023 unmarried and issueless.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Ajith Silva up to the present owners in relation to the property bearing Assessment No. 12, Temple Road, Nugegoda. **(20 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(5 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

Under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, a surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property.

claims.text: Under the Stamp Duty Act 1982 and the Western Province Financial Statute 1990, when property is gifted subject to a reservation in favour of the donor or another person, the stamp duty is calculated on the value of the property as if it had been gifted without that reservation. However, there is no information regarding the specific valuation positions before and after 31 March 1977.

The stamp duty on the Deed of Gift from Mark Perera to Peter Perera must be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if it had been gifted without the reservation of the life interest, but the exact stamp duty payable cannot be computed because the stamp duty rate schedule is missing.

hits.excerpt: 48. (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. (2) Where any property transferred for a consideration is subject to any mortgage, encumbrances or reservation of interest, stamp duty with which the instrument of transfer is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property transferred, without any deduction for the mortgage, encumbrances or reservation. (3) Where any property is gifted subject to any reservation in favour of the donor or any other person, stamp duty with which the instrument of gift is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if that property had been gifted to the donee without that reservation.

Where any instrument is chargeable with stamp duty in Conversion respect of any money expressed in any currency other than that of Sri Lanka, such duty shall be calculated of the value of such money in the currency of Sri Lanka according to the current rate of exchange on the day of the date of the instrument or where the instrument is a bill of exchange, cheque or promissory note drawn or made, out of Sri Lanka, on the day on which the instrument is stamped in Sri Lanka. 12

Mala is living with her daughter in Kurunegala. She intends to lease her own house in Colombo to Sheela for a monthly rental of Rs. 100,000 for two years. The rental is payable on the 20th day of each month, commencing in 2020. Mala obtained a refundable deposit of Rs. 300,000 from Sheela. She also obtained an advance payment of Rs. 600,000 and intends it to be set off against the first year’s monthly rental.

2. How much will Sheela have to pay as monthly rental during the first year? **(2 marks)**
3. Mala intends to visit her son in Australia. Mala gave a Special Power of Attorney to her daughter Visaka in 2017 to sell the house in Colombo. Can Visaka execute the lease agreement with Sheela on behalf of Mala if Mala travels to Australia? Advise Mala on how to execute the lease agreement in her absence. **(5 marks)**

claims.text: Under Section 24(c) of the Stamp Duty Act, 1982, the stamp duty on a lease or agreement to lease is payable by the lessee or intended lessee (Sheela), unless there is an agreement to the contrary. However, the precise calculation of the stamp duty cannot be performed because the applicable rate schedule is missing from the provided statutes.

Under Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance, a power of attorney is a written authority given by one person to another to perform any work or do any act. Since Visaka's 2017 Special Power of Attorney is restricted to selling the Colombo house, she does not have the authority to execute a lease agreement, and Mala must grant a new power of attorney specifically for leasing.

If Mala executes the new power of attorney in Sri Lanka, Section 3A of the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act, No. 28 of 2022 requires that it be duly attested by a notary public and contain a description of the land with its metes, bounds, and extent.

If Mala executes the power of attorney while abroad, Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance (as amended by Section 2 of the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act, No. 3 of 2024) allows a power of attorney to be executed before or attested by an Ambassador, High Commissioner, or other diplomatic representative of Sri Lanka.

4. Nimal is the caretaker of land parcel 006 in Cadastral Plan No. 521521 situated in Homagama. The property belongs to Kamal, who is working in Australia. Kamal visits Sri Lanka annually. claims.text: Under section 44 of the Registration of Title Act, a Notary Public attesting an instrument must: (a) satisfy himself of the identity of unknown parties and witnesses using official identity cards or other reliable means; (b) satisfy himself of the capacity of the parties by referring to the Title Registry records or an extract from the relevant Title Register; and (c) satisfy himself of the identity of the land and state of the title by reference to the Certificate of Title and Title Registry records.

claims.text: Under the Notaries Ordinance, as amended, a notary must not execute or attest: (1) any deed or instrument written on ola; (2) any deed or instrument written on paper that is not of a reasonably durable description; (3) any deed or instrument written on more than one entire or undivided parchment paper or blue sheet unless either each sheet is pre-marked/signed/initialled by the Registrar of Lands of the notary's district, or both the executing parties and the notary sign every sheet and the pages are numbered; and (4) he must not sign his name or make his mark upon any paper intended for his protocol or a draft/copy until the entire deed or instrument has been written or engrossed thereon.

To obtain the annual certificate to practice, a notary must deliver: (1) a written declaration signed by him stating his name, place(s) of residence, the exact situation of his office(s), and the judicial zone of practice; and (2) an annexed affidavit stating that he forwarded all duplicates of deeds/instruments attested by him in the previous year to the Registrar of Lands and that any money imposed by the Registrar-General under section 35 has been paid. The exact deadline date for this submission is not specified in the retrieved text.
A notary must affix passport-size photographs of the signatories (excluding witnesses) to the protocol for a deed of transfer, a deed of gift, a deed of exchange, or a will.

claims.text: Under the Apartment Ownership Law, a Condominium Plan must contain a declaration in the prescribed form made by the applicant and attested by a Notary Public. This declaration must include: a reference-based description of the land's boundaries, extent, and situation; the name and address of the property owners; particulars of title deeds, instruments, and registration details under the Registration of Documents Ordinance; particulars of any known encumbrances or lis pendens; a description of the building's storeys, basements, and units; unit details such as floor area, room count, and accessory units; a description of the common elements and the percentage of undivided share appurtenant to each unit; restrictions on use; and the signatures of the owners.

Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**

4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

question:
Gamini Perera was allotted Lot A depicted in Partition Plan No. 2525 dated 2 February 1981, made by S. Silva, Licensed Surveyor, bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama, containing in extent 10 perches, by a final decree of a partition case bearing No. 111/P dated 2 February 1985 entered in the District Court of Homagama.

Gamini Perera, by Deed of Gift No. 515 dated 10 March 1986, attested by R. Liyanage, Notary Public, gifted the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 absolutely and irrevocably to his son, Suresh Perera, subject to the life interest of Gamini Perera and his wife Vinitha. Gamini Perera died on 12 June 1990 due to heart failure. Vinitha revoked her life interest over the said Lot A depicted in Plan No. 2525 by Deed of Revocation of Life Interest No. 525 dated 25 February 1991, attested by S. Sapumal, Notary Public.

Suresh Perera married Kanthi and had two children, namely Rakitha and Muditha. Muditha died due to an accident on 5 June 2023, unmarried and issueless. Rakitha married Ann and died on 2 July 2022.

Suresh Perera died on 10 December 1995 intestate. Suresh Perera had an offspring named Samantha from his first marriage, who is a citizen of the United States of America.

1. Draw up the pedigree showing the devolution of title from Gamini Perera up to the present owners in relation to the land and premises bearing Assessment No. 20, Flower Road, Homagama. **(15 marks)**
2. What are the shares presently owned by each heir in the property? **(4 marks)**
3. Can Samantha become entitled to the intestate estate of Suresh Perera? Discuss with reference to the provisions of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014, as amended by the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) (Amendment) Act No. 21 of 2018. **(2 marks)**
4. Explain the rules set out in sections 22 to 26 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. **(4 marks)**

**Total: 25 marks**

claims.text: Although stamp duty is generally calculated on the value of the property conveyed without deductions (as seen in Western Province Financial Statute s48), the specific rate of stamp duty for a Deed of Transfer of land in Galle (Southern Province) is not specified in the provided texts, making the calculation of the payable stamp duty on Rs. 100,000,000 impossible.

The stamp duty on the instrument must be paid prior to, or at the time of, the execution of the instrument. The mode of payment is by means of affixing adhesive stamps or impressed stamps to the required value; alternatively, if it is not practicable to use stamps, payment can be made to the Commissioner General who will endorse the payment on the instrument. The specific payment location or prescribed bank for land transfers in the Southern Province is not provided.

hits.excerpt: 48. (1) Where any property is conveyed by an instrument, the stamp duty with which such instrument is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property conveyed. (2) Where any property transferred for a consideration is subject to any mortgage, encumbrances or reservation of interest, stamp duty with which the instrument of transfer is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property transferred, without any deduction for the mortgage, encumbrances or reservation. (3) Where any property is gifted subject to any reservation in favour of the donor or any other person, stamp duty with which the instrument of gift is chargeable shall be calculated on the value of the property gifted as if that property had been gifted to the donee without that reservation.

> **Note:** This page was blurred. The wording below is reconstructed from the visible text.

A Notary who has practised in Homagama since approximately 1987 intends to apply for appointment/registration under the Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998 and other relevant written law.

1. How do the requirements under the relevant law apply to the Commissioner of Title Settlement and to what types of land would title be registered? **(4 marks)**
2. Could both the owner and occupier make an application in respect of the land? Can the application be rejected without an inquiry? **(4 marks)**
3. A deed affecting land is executed, but the instrument is not presented for registration within the prescribed period. Is registration mandatory, and what is the legal consequence of non-registration? **(4 marks)**
4. Who may present an instrument for registration according to the Registration of Title Act/Registration of Documents Ordinance? **(3 marks)**

**Total: 15 marks**

claims.text: Upon receiving certified copies of cadastral maps, the Commissioner of Title Settlement is required to publish a Notice in the Gazette calling for claimants to the specified land parcel to submit their claims within a prescribed period.

A District Court may make an order of Declaration of Title in favor of a claimant to the whole land parcel or to a divided portion, provided that divided portion does not fall below the prescribed minimum extent.

While the law permits the Commissioner to call for claims from claimants, the retrieved sections do not contain any provisions specifying whether both an owner and occupier can make an application, or whether an application can be rejected without an inquiry.
The provided sections do not state that registration of a deed affecting land is mandatory.

An unregistered instrument executed or made on or after January 1, 1864, is void against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered.
Fraud or collusion in obtaining a subsequent instrument or in securing its prior registration defeats the priority of the person claiming under it.
Registration of an instrument does not cure any defect in the instrument or confer upon it any effect or validity other than the priority conferred by section 7.

The Registration of Documents Ordinance acknowledges that registration is initiated by 'the person who presented it for registration or his agent', without further defining who is authorized to do so for ordinary deeds.
A caveator who has or claims to have a right, title, or interest to a land, undivided land, land parcel, or condominium parcel may present a caveat for registration.

claims.text: Under the provided provisions, specific persons authorized to present documents include: a judgment creditor who may present a seizure priority notice (SRC005:s31(1)), and a caveator (a person who has or claims to have a right, title, or interest to a land, undivided land, land parcel, or condominium parcel) who may present a caveat (SRC009:s32(1)(a)). The ordinance also refers generally to an authorized person or their agent presenting an instrument, though the general definition of authorized presenters is not fully detailed in the provided sections.

Under the Ordinance, a Registrar may refuse to register an instrument if they suspect the presenter is not authorized until the right to present is proved, or if the instrument does not comply with the Ordinance or any written law affecting its form or mode of execution. Additionally, a Registrar is mandated to refuse registration if the instrument is liable to stamp duty but is not duly stamped, or until any registration fee is paid.

If an error or omission is shown to the satisfaction of the Registrar-General, they must issue a written notice in the prescribed form: (a) to the parties for a deed, (b) to the executor or administrator for a will, or (c) to the presenter for other instruments, and order the correction. The correction is made by the relevant Registrar in the prescribed manner without affecting prior accrued priority. Notice may be dispensed with if death, legal incapacity, or other sufficient cause prevents issuance. If the error and correction are in different folios, they must be cross-referenced. A person aggrieved by a refusal to make a correction order may sue in the District Court within 30 days of the communication of the refusal.

hits.excerpt: Seizure property 31. (1) When a writ of execution is issued, the judgment creditor may, so long notices. as the judgment remains unsatisfied, present for registration a notice (in this Ordinance called a 'seizure priority notice') to the effect that the land described therein is liable to seizure under the writ of execution. (2) If, at any time while the seizure priority notice remains in force, notice of seizure of any land described in the seizure priority notice is registered, notice of the seizure shall, for the purposes of this Ordinance and of section 238 of the Civil Procedure Code, be deemed to have been registered at the time of registration of the seizure priority notice or at the time when the seizure was actually effected, whichever date shall be the later, and shall have effect accordingly. (3) The Registrar shall, on receiving a seizure priority notice, register it in the same manner as other instruments, but shall retain the notice. (4) A seizure priority notice shall remain in force for six weeks from the date of registration of the notice, but may, at any time before the end of such six weeks, be renewed for a further period of six weeks, and if so renewed shall remain in force for a further period of six weeks computed from the end of the first period of six weeks. (5) If notice of a seizure under the writ of execution is not registered while the seizure priority notice remains in force, the seizure priority notice shall be deemed to have lapsed and shall have no effect under the provisions of this Ordinance.

claims.text: Under the Apartment Ownership (Special Provisions) Act, No. 23 of 2018, owners of certain registered condominium properties must submit a written declaration from the Director-General of the Department of Buildings certifying the safety of occupation of the property.

The provisions mention a 'Condominium Plan' and a 'Plan of redivision or amalgamation', which can be registered or amended, but do not provide further definitions of distinct types of plans or the differences between them.

Section 24 contains a heading stating 'Provisions of Partition Act not to apply in certain cases', but the substantive text explaining the details of this restriction is not contained in the provided text.

# Sri Lanka Law College – Conveyancing (LW 307)

claims.text: Yes, Martin Perera can execute the Will and exclude his children without assigning any reason. Under Section 2(2) of the Wills Ordinance (as substituted by the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022), every testator has full power to make testamentary dispositions as they see fit, including the right to exclude, disinherit, or omit any child, parent, relative, or descendant without assigning any reason.

According to Section 2(1) of the Wills Ordinance (as substituted by the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022), the explicit statutory requirements are that the person executing the will must have reached eighteen years of age, may reside within or outside Sri Lanka, can dispose of property belonging to them at the time of death (which would otherwise devolve to heirs), and the beneficiary must not be legally incapacitated from receiving it. Additionally, Section 4 of the Wills Ordinance was repealed by Section 4 of the Wills (Amendment) Act No. 29 of 2022.

The provided statutory provisions do not specify the steps an executor must take after the death of a sole testator. The only procedural instruction provided states that upon the demise of a testator in a joint last will, testamentary proceedings must be instituted under Chapter XXXVIII or Chapter XXXVIIIB of the Civil Procedure Code to obtain probate or letters of administration with the will annexed.

The provided texts of the Notaries Ordinance, as amended, do not contain or specify any mandatory clause that a Notary must include in the attestation of a Last Will. The provisions only outline administrative duties, such as listing only the number and date of wills and codicils in the monthly list (and omitting executor names in the weekly list) delivered to the Registrar of Lands.
